name: /api/health must report AI readiness (provider, configured, reachable)
description:
WRITTEN FROM: codx-junior-website (hosted provisioning, server/services/installer.js + installScript.js). We provision the box, hand the settings file to your installer, and then have to tell a customer "your workspace is ready". Today we cannot: /api/health proves the PROCESS is alive, not that the workspace can do anything.

OBSERVED (real instance, measured 2026-11-22)

GET https://e2e-live-1122.codx-junior.ai/api/health -> 200
{"status":"ok","version":"0.0.1","ref":"v0.0.1-1-gdba24f4","commit":"dba24f4bf27c…","uptime_seconds":4055.3,"event_loop_lag_ms":{"last_ms":0.9,"max_ms":1612.5},"projects_cached":1,"api_log_pipeline":{…}}

- there is NO field describing the AI backend: not the provider, not the model, not whether it is configured, not whether it can be reached
- GET /api/config/ai -> 404 (no supported endpoint either)
- the only way to know is to log in as a human and try to talk to it — which is exactly what a hosting pipeline cannot do for every customer workspace

WHY THIS BITES US (concrete, not hypothetical)

Our deployment contract lets a workspace be created with `CODX_JUNIOR_AI_PROVIDER` set and `CODX_JUNIOR_AI_API_KEY` empty (allowed today: a local model server needs no key — see DEPLOYMENT-CONTRACT.md §1, `[verified]` "any non-empty value for a local server that does not check it"). A machine provisioned that way installs, serves 200 on :19981, passes our readiness probe and reports `status: ok` — while it cannot answer a single message. We shipped exactly that in our first live E2E: the box is green by every signal we can read from outside, and it is brain-dead for the customer.

The same blindness hits support: when a customer says "the AI does not answer", we cannot even tell which provider/model the box thinks it is using without shell access to the instance.

WHAT WE ASK

A. Add an `ai` block to /api/health (documented in DEPLOYMENT-CONTRACT.md §? next to the provenance fields), e.g.:
   "ai": { "provider": "ollama", "model": "…", "configured": true, "reachable": false, "checked_at": "2026-11-22T17:00:00Z" }
   - `configured` = a provider is selected and the credential/endpoint it needs is present
   - `reachable` = a cheap liveness probe of the configured endpoint succeeded (cached, e.g. <=30 s, never a billable completion; a HEAD/GET /models on an OpenAI-compatible endpoint is enough)
   - never echo the key or any part of it

B. Make readiness explicit for machines: either degrade `status` to "degraded" when `ai.configured && !ai.reachable`, or expose a documented `ready` boolean that covers both "process alive" and "AI usable". We will gate our `install_done` step on it either way — we just need one field that means "this workspace can work".

C. Keep it non-fatal for a box with no AI at all: `am I reachable by a browser and does my data plane answer` must stay distinguishable from `my model server is down`, so an operator can still see the difference.

ACCEPTANCE
- GET /api/health on a workspace with a live provider: ai.configured true, ai.reachable true, ai.provider/model filled, no secret in the payload
- GET /api/health on a workspace whose provider endpoint is unreachable: ai.reachable false within one cache window, `status`/`ready` reflecting it
- documented in codx-junior-installer/cloud/DEPLOYMENT-CONTRACT.md so hosting providers can rely on it

OUR SIDE (already done)
- server/services/installScript.js writes CODX_JUNIOR_AI_PROVIDER/MODEL/API_URL and the key only when present; the key is never logged and never lands in db.json
- our `install_done` step already polls the published port and, since this week, verifies TLS instead of asserting it; the AI check is the missing half of "ready"
